ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 and its Regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9; Alberta Corporate Registry Regulations, Alta. Reg. 95/2021; Canada Business Corporations Act (if federal cross-border structural review is required). The Alberta corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and file the annual Corporation Information Return, with mandatory disclosure of UBO details to FINTRAC and securities regulators on request.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and UBOS against the consolidated Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, regulations under the United Nations Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, FINTRAC published guidance, OFAC SDN list (because USD ACH and bank-wire rails are used), and UN Security Council sanctions. Mandatory enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign PEPs, including family members and close associates. Automated daily re-screening is required for the equity crowdfunding portal environment. The Alberta Securities Commission registration process mandates personal background checks, statutory declarations, and suitability reviews for directors and officers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registration System (CORES) / Service Alberta (online Name Request portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French using Roman script characters; non-Roman names must be transliterated and accompanied by a certified translation. The name must include a distinctive element and a mandatory legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Limited'. Alberta does not permit non-Roman characters in the corporate name field.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request a written reconsideration from the Director of Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness, the written consent of any party whose name is allegedly conflicting, or a court order supporting the name. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue administrative review before the Registrar and thereafter judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. A fresh name reservation filing is also permitted in parallel with the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may satisfy the Alberta statutory registered office requirement where it is a physical street address in Alberta and is staffed during normal business hours. However, for an ISIC 6499 equity crowdfunding portal, the Alberta Securities Commission and FINTRAC expect a substantive business office, not merely a virtual mailing address. A registered physical office in Alberta, accessible records, and a responsible officer in Canada will be required for licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70-85% risk of unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months after FINTRAC registration and Alberta Securities Commission licensing; unannounced compliance examinations are routine for crowdfunding portals and money-service-business-like intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 6, 9, 10, 12, 15, 101-106, 210; Corporations Information Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c C-29, s 4; Income Tax Act (Canada), RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), s 241.1 (CRA Business Number)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), Corporate Registry Division, 7th Floor Commerce Place, 10155-102 Street, Edmonton, AB T5J 4G1; online e-filing via ABCorporate Online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (electronic ABCA form) together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, submitted through ABCorporate Online and certified by the Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; incorporation may proceed with one or more no-par-value common shares and no escrowed capital deposit. Escrow trust account requirements arise only upon receipt of investor contributions under Alberta securities crowdfunding rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Board of Directors of [Company Name] Inc. accepts and allots the common shares set out in Schedule A, ratifying all subscription agreements executed prior to incorporation. FURTHER RESOLVED: The registered office is established at Suite 2100, 888 3rd Street SW, Calgary, Alberta T2P 5C5, Canada; the directors appoint [Registered Agent] as registered agent for service. FURTHER RESOLVED: [Name] is elected Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Compliance Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED: The officers are authorized to open escrow and operating bank accounts, execute the Alberta Securities Commission funding-portal registration application, and complete FINTRAC money-services business registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), ABCorporate Online portal and registered NUANS service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS Name Search Report request for a proposed Alberta business corporation name. Verify distinctiveness against federal and provincial databases; confirm the legal element 'Inc.,' 'Corp.,' or 'Ltd.' is included; ensure no reserved or prohibited terms such as 'Bank,' 'Trust,' or 'Insurance' appear without a separate license. Secure a 90-day name reservation hold.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report request form
Proposed corporate name and legal element declaration
Director identification and consent records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusing, file a revised NUANS application with an alternate distinctive element; request registry re-scrutiny under the Corporations Information Act within 21 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), ABCorporate Online e-filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete electronic Articles of Incorporation together with initial Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors; validate director consent signatures; pay the C$250 consolidation fee (name search plus incorporation) by credit card; submit via ABCorporate Online; download the electronically issued Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (electronic ABCA form)
NUANS Name Search Report with reservation number
Notice of Registered Office
Notice of Directors and director consent forms
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry clarification queries are corrected and re-submitted electronically within 5 business days; if rejected for substantive defects, refile promptly while retaining the NUANS 90-day name priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Kit and By-laws Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office administration and Alberta Corporate Registry records branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the corporate minute book; adopt By-law No. 1 covering board meetings, share transfers, and indemnification; issue share certificates; execute an organizational board resolution ratifying officers; file the statutory initial returns within the ABCA deadline windows.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
By-law No. 1 (general corporate by-law)
Share certificates and share register
Organizational board meeting minutes
Registered office acceptance form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incorrect notices are revoked and refiled through ABCorporate Online; late-filing penalty relief may be obtained by delivering a written explanation to the Registry within 30 days of the missed deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Federal Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a CRA Business Number (BN) and open the corporate income tax account; concurrently elect to register for GST/HST if annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed C$30,000; open a payroll program account if employees will be hired; verify director identity and registered office data through online authentication.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address and mailing address
Director legal names, SINs where applicable, and date of birth
Estimated annual revenue and GST/HST election form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA identity verification errors are cured via e-service correspondence; account corrections are processed using Form RC273 after telephone authentication with CRA business enquiries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Securities Commission (ASC), Registration Department, 600-400 3rd Avenue SW, Calgary, AB T2P 4H2
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal restricted-dealer registration application through the ASC National Registration Database (NRD), designating the corporation as an equity crowdfunding funding portal; file individual registration forms for the CEO and Chief Compliance Officer; attach the compliance manual, escrow custody agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank, business continuity plan, and audited financial statement or start-up capital statement.
required_dossiers: ASC restricted-dealer registration application and Form 33-109F6
Individual Form 33-109F5 and form of registration for CEO and CCO
Compliance manual and supervisory procedures
Escrow agreement with Canadian bank for investor funds
Business continuity and cybersecurity incident response plan
Privacy policy aligned with Alberta Personal Information Protection Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to ASC deficiency letters within 20 days with supplemental material; if registration is refused, exercise the right to a hearing under Part 2 of the Securities Act (Alberta) and amend the business model or capital structure to comply with crowdfunding limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), Compliance and Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation as a Money Services Business (MSB) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) because escrow disbursements and investor fund transfers constitute money services activity; complete the online MSB registration, disclose all places of business, executive officers, and the compliance regimen, and appoint a compliance officer.
required_dossiers: FINTRAC MSB registration application
Compliance program summary including policies and procedures
Risk assessment matrix and anti-money laundering/terrorist financing risk model
List of all places of business and service channels
Compliance officer appointment record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: FINTRAC clarification requests are answered by supplementary filing within 30 days; deficient registrations may be amended online, and failure to register is an offence that may be cured by prompt rectification and voluntary disclosure before the submission of false or misleading data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Physical Office Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Licensing Department (or City of Edmonton) and local municipal fire marshal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a City of Calgary Business Licence classified as a Financial Technology Intermediary; obtain a Certificate of Occupancy from the Municipal Building Department; arrange an Alberta Fire Code inspection of the office premises; post OHS notices and register a workplace harassment and violence prevention plan with the occupational health and safety program.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application and fee payment
Certificate of Incorporation and lease agreement
Alberta Fire Code fire safety inspection certificate
Certificate of Occupancy for the office suite
OHS hazard assessment and first-aid compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal deficiency notices are cured by remedial reinspection within 14 days; occupancy classification disputes may be appealed to the City subdivision and development appeal board for a revised certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission (ASC) as the competent securities licensing authority for equity crowdfunding portals, supplemented by the municipal business licensing department and FINTRAC for anti-money-laundering oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Restricted Dealer Registration (Equity Crowdfunding Funding Portal) under the Securities Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c S-4, Part 2, together with the City of Calgary Business Licence for Financial Technology Intermediary

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Regulatory Assurance Division); federal counterpart Environment and Climate Change Canada for matters of interprovincial electronic data infrastructure
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class C administrative commercial occupancy; no mandatory environmental impact assessment; no Schedule B listed activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3 for a digital financial intermediary office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge applies; office operations must comply with municipal wastewater sewer-use bylaws (City of Calgary Wastewater Bylaw 24M2021), Alberta Recycling Management Authority e-waste handling rules for electronic equipment disposal, and applicable electrical safety standards; no VOC, GHG, or particulate thresholds attach to office-only activities

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code (NFC 2019 with Alberta amendments) for the office suite; barrier-free design compliance under the Alberta Building Code 2019; structural load inspection and Certificate of Occupancy for the server-room floor rating; annual occupational health and safety hazard assessment, first-aid kit certification, and workplace violence and harassment prevention plan under the OHS Act (Alberta); evacuation route signage and emergency lighting certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – My Business Account portal (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-individuals/business-account.html); Alberta Corporate Registry for provincial incorporation; Corporations Canada for federal incorporation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Canadian federal Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or using CRA Business Registration Online (BRO). The BN is the umbrella identifier for all tax accounts, including the GST/HST account, corporate income tax account, and payroll deduction account. If the entity is incorporated in Alberta, it must register with the Alberta Corporate Registry; if federally incorporated and carrying on business in Alberta, it must complete extra-provincial registration. The non-resident corporation may register directly online or appoint an authorized agent with written authorization. The CRA may require proof of a Canadian address or third-party service address for service of notices. Upon registration, the CRA issues a BN plus a two-letter program account suffix (e.g., RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box regime exists. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Excise Tax Act, available elections include: section 216 election for non-resident corporations deriving rental income or timber royalties; section 219 branch tax election; section 273 of the Excise Tax Act for GST/HST election between closely related corporations to simplify reporting; election for eligible intercompany supplies; and hybrid mismatch adjustments under the Income Tax Act (including s. 163.2 penalties) implementing BEPS Action 2. Provincial tax elections follow federal T2-based calculations; Alberta does not impose a separate capital tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax; Alberta imposes only the 5% federal GST, with no provincial sales tax or HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) calculated over any trailing four consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents making no taxable supplies to recipients in Canada other than zero-rated exports are generally not required to register, but may voluntarily register under the Excise Tax Act for input tax credit recovery; once registered, the entity remains required to file GST/HST returns even if supplies fall below threshold, until revocation is approved.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or API-based digital stamping regime applies. Electronic invoicing is permitted, but every GST/HST invoice must contain prescribed information under section 3 of the Excise Tax Act Regulations, including supplier BN, recipient business name, transaction date, description, tax amount, and tax rate. Filing is electronic via GST/HST NETFILE or EDI for registrants. Digital record-keeping and CRA audit access to electronic books are mandatory. Certain industries operate under CRA-issued electronic filing specifications, but the crowdfunding portal is not subject to real-time invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act applies to supplies of goods exported by the supplier (s. 1 of Part V of Schedule VI), supplies of services performed wholly outside Canada (s. 7), and supplies of services provided to a non-resident person that are not in connection with real property in Canada or a taxable supply in Canada (s. 1 of Part V, Schedule VII). For an equity crowdfunding portal, platform service fees charged to non-resident issuers are typically zero-rated if the service is supplied to a non-resident and the service does not relate to making a taxable supply in Canada. The portal must obtain a written declaration, business registration evidence, and residential or place-of-business proof from each non-resident recipient. For goods exported, the exporter must demonstrate physical export within a reasonable time; for services, contemporaneous documentation must show where the service was performed and for whom.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export declaration (B13A or approved electronic equivalent)
Commercial invoice with zero-rating notation and HST exemption clause
Bill of lading, waybill, or freight forwarder's cargo receipt
Inward remittance certificate / bank transfer confirmation evidencing foreign proceeds
Signed service agreement with the non-resident issuer or counterparty
Foreign exchange buy/sell contract and payment ledger
Proof of non-resident status (certificate of incorporation, tax ID, or residency declaration)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA routinely scrutinizes zero-rating claims through matching customs export data, banking inflows, and service agreements. A denied zero-rating results in reassessment of GST/HST plus interest (prescribed rate compounded daily), reinstatement of penalties under Excise Tax Act section 280 (failure to file), section 281.1 (false or misleading statements), and gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the tax avoided. Companies face interest under the Income Tax Act for unreported taxable amounts, prosecution for wilful evasion, levy on unremitted taxes, and director liability under the Excise Tax Act. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims are retroactively clawed back for the entire audit period and may trigger criminal referral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration shared with the Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for transaction monitoring and reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a fully convertible currency under a floating exchange-rate regime. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are free from exchange-control restrictions, including profit remittances, dividend distributions, and foreign direct investment returns. No prior regulatory approval is required for repatriation. Financial institutions must report electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and issuers must comply with withholding tax and securities-law disclosure obligations on distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export receipts. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts with domestic banks without restriction, subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds and anti-money-laundering recordkeeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate to high for licensed Canadian money services businesses (MSBs) and non-bank payment service providers that are registered with FINTRAC and, where applicable, hold a provincial money lender or payment-services licence. Offshore digital EMIs without Canadian registration may provide cross-border payout services only on a passive cross-border basis, but active solicitation or settlement of Canadian retail crowdfunding investors requires a domestic MSB registration and compliance with National Instrument 45-110 (NI 45-110) and applicable Alberta securities laws. Use of an offshore EMI as the sole settlement rail is legally constrained and operationally risky; a Canadian-registered MSB or a Schedule I bank with escrow-capable trust accounts is preferred.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for Canadian business corporations using secure video identity verification, corporate record reviews, and electronic signatures. For a high-risk equity crowdfunding portal, tier-one banks typically require a live video interview with the director or authorized signatory, enhanced beneficial-ownership attestations, and legal-counsel certification. Physical branch presence is not categorically mandated for Canadian-incorporated entities, but an in-person notarization or bank branch attendance may be imposed as a mitigation condition during enhanced due diligence review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership due to layered corporate structures or nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry abstract, organizational chart, shareholder register, statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership, certified identity documents of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, trust deed or nominee agreement if applicable, and a written explanation of control chain submitted under Alberta corporate law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding investor source of funds and source of wealth cannot be verified
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor bank statements for a reasonable period (commonly 90 days), completed source-of-funds questionnaire, tax assessment notice or proof of salary, signed subscription agreement, AML/KYC identity documentation collected under NI 45-110 and FINTRAC requirements, and a log of verification checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification as a non-bank crowdfunding intermediary without evident licensing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of registration or exemption as a funding portal or exempt market dealer under Alberta Securities Commission rules, a copy of NI 45-110 offering documents, the escrow arrangement with a qualified trust company or bank, proof of FINTRAC MSB registration (if applicable), and a copy of the issuer's offering memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers from or to high-risk or FATF-listed jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction purpose codes, counterparty due-diligence file, enhanced negative-news and PEP screening results, documented economic rationale, contract or subscription documents, and board-approved risk assessment with per-transaction audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large cash or wire transaction thresholds triggering FINTRAC reportable event
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-formatted large cash transaction report (LCTR) and electronic funds transfer report (EFTR), internal compliance procedure sign-off, risk-based assessment, and timestamped audit trail demonstrating no structuring or evasion of the CAD 10,000 threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign-currency or CAD capital contributions from investors must be remitted by wire to a segregated escrow account in Canada held by a licensed bank or trust company, with the investor name, offering name, and subscription reference included in the SWIFT MT103 beneficiary information. The bank account title must clearly indicate escrow/trust status. FINTRAC registers all electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Fund origin, beneficial owner, and source-of-wealth documentation must be verified before acceptance. For non-resident investors, no exchange-control approval is needed, but the reverse side of the offering documents must confirm compliance with Canada's foreign-investor tax and securities exemptions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement payments to vendors, service providers, and refunded investors use SWIFT MT103 payment messages for fiat transfers via correspondent banking corridors, and SWIFT MT202 for interbank or nostro account transfers. Commercial letters of credit are used for trade-linked disbursements with the issuing bank receiving compliant presentation documentation. Escrowed crowdfunding proceeds may only be disbursed upon legal closing conditions, using dual-authorization controls, pre-noted beneficiary account validation, and transaction-level audit reporting to the regulator if demanded.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts traded with an authorized Canadian financial institution or licensed derivatives dealer
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts where CAD or the target currency is non-deliverable, executed under a negotiated ISDA master agreement
Cross-currency swap contracts for aligning token- or share-proceeds settlement currencies with operating expenses
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX options for capped protection on large conversion flows, subject to internal derivatives risk policy and board approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (or Extra-Provincial Annual Return for a federal corporation registered in Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or registration; annual thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 per return; continued non-filing for three consecutive years allows administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta corporate income tax administered by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; annual thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; if no balance owing, a flat penalty of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500; interest accrues on unpaid tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, every private corporation must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting, but the audit requirement may be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution (ABCA s. 170); no revenue/asset threshold applies to private non-offering corporations. If the entity holds an exempt market dealer or crowdfunding-portal registration with the Alberta Securities Commission, annual audited financial statements are mandatory under National Instrument 31-103.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) in accordance with the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is mandatory if the corporation is a reporting issuer or if required by securities regulation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO return is filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry; the ABCA annual return confirms the current directors and registered office. Registered share transfers must be recorded in the securities register at the time of transfer, and, for a federal CBCA corporation or a portal subject to securities regulation, the register of individuals with significant control must be updated within 15 days of any change. If the annual return jurisdiction is a federal corporation, the ISC register is inspected at the registered office but not filed with Corporations Canada on an annual basis.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (if governed by CBCA or ASC AML/registration requirements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – 750 per year for a registered office/agent service in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 15,000 per year for an audited private corporation with crowdfunding-portal activity; actual fees vary by transaction volume and ASC reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal general corporate income tax + 8% Alberta general corporate income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) may apply the small business deduction: federal rate reduced to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, combined with Alberta's 2% small business rate for an aggregate 11% effective rate. Additional relief includes the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (refundable/non-refundable up to 35%), clean technology and digital adoption incentives, and Alberta innovation tax credits for qualifying activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including Alberta supplementary schedules, filed electronically via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) My Business Account portal or approved third-party software; mandatory for all resident corporations and non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal period-end. The balance-due day for taxes is generally the last day of the 3rd month after fiscal year-end for a CCPC, and the 2nd month after fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs. Quarterly instalments are required for large corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, commissions, or fees from revenue generated by the crowdfunding portal, including issuance fees, admin fees, and platform transaction fees, net of refunds and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations report only Canadian-source gross revenue derived from the portal's activities; expenses reasonably incurred may be allocated on a proportionate basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all statutory adjustments, including deductions for eligible expenses, capital cost allowances, non-capital losses carried forward, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same computation limited to Canadian-source income; transfer-pricing adjustments are allowed only if they reflect arm's-length dealings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial corporate income tax calculated on the Alberta schedule: 8% general rate, or 2% for the first CAD 500,000 of eligible CCPC active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Alberta taxable income based on the prescribed permanent-establishment formula (Schedule A5) if the non-resident has a qualifying permanent establishment in Alberta.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; repeated failure to file an additional 10% federal penalty; late-payment interest compounded daily at the CRA prescribed rate; gross negligence penalties up to 50% of unreported income; additional penalties under s.162(2) and s.162(7) for non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced withholding under an applicable Canada tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a fully completed Form NR301-A, NR301, or NR302 (or a valid Certificate of Residence issued by the treaty jurisdiction) to the Canadian withholding agent before payment. The payer must retain the form and attach it to the annual T4/T5 summary if applicable. For payments routed through an intermediary, the beneficial-owner status must be certified. Without a valid claim, the statutory 25% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties (patent, trademark, software, know-how) and 25% for interest paid to non-arm's-length non-residents, with limited exemptions for certain arm's-length interest obligations. Treaty rates under the Canada–US, Canada–UK, and typical OECD-based DTAs are commonly: royalties 10% (often 0% for copyright on cultural works), interest 10% (or fully exempt for arm's-length financial institutions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million aggregated non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents in the fiscal year triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (Local File) and Form T106 filing; Master File documentation becomes mandatory for taxpayers whose consolidated group gross revenue exceeds CAD 20 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute as in low-tax jurisdictions, but the CRA applies the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty-benefit denial, and recharacterisation principles where a corporation lacks commercial substance. An equity crowdfunding portal must demonstrate real Alberta presence: leased office, resident directors/managers, active board meetings, executed vendor agreements, payroll, and the required securities licences and controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of portal fee income, fabrication of expenses, transfer of profits to an unconnected related shell company at non-arm's-length prices, or the coordinated failure to remit payroll source deductions and GST/HST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act: on indictment, penalties of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years (summary conviction: up to 2 years); civil penalty under s.163(2) of the greater of 50% of evaded tax and CAD 4,000; interest accrues daily on arrears; the CRA may re-audit and issue levy against assets. The Alberta Securities Commission may simultaneously revoke the portal registration and issue administrative fines up to CAD 2 million per contravention.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST pursuant to s.227.1 of the Income Tax Act. Where fraud or fraudulent preference is proven, the Alberta Business Corporations Act allows a court to pierce the corporate veil, rendering directors personally liable for civil damages, restitution, and award costs. Criminal directors face imprisonment, asset-seizure and formal travel bans while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the crowdfunding portal as a letterbox entity with no real place of management in Alberta, all strategic decisions taken abroad, no local employees, no registered bank account or physical premises, and profits stripped via a bare royalty or management-fee arrangement to a related foreign entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may deny expense deductions, recharacterise revenue under GAAR, reallocate income under Canada's transfer-pricing rules (s.247), and assess default penalties of 10% of gross transfer-pricing adjustment. Alberta’s securities regulator may suspend or cancel the exempt-market dealer or crowdfunding licence for failure to maintain a head office and essential staff; corporate registration may be cancelled for failure to return a statutory declaration or file annual returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be named in CRA director-liability assessments for taxes, interest, and penalties arising from unremitted withheld amounts. Courts will disregard the corporate separation if the corporation is a façade for personal liability or if directors personally controlled the route of funds; civil judgments may include disgorgement, freezing orders, and, in cases of fraud, imprisonment of up to 14 years under s.380 of the Criminal Code for fraud over CAD 1 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating ACH escrow and bank-wire payment rails without a registered money services business or AML/CFT programme; failure to conduct verify of crowdfunding investors, no ongoing beneficial-ownership checks, no monitoring for suspicious transactions, and no filing of Suspicious Transaction Reports with FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 10 million per violation for corporations (and up to CAD 2 million for individuals) per occurrence; further CRA penalties for unregistered MSB activity; the Alberta Securities Commission may impose cease-trade orders and license revocation; FINTRAC may publish the violation and impose cross-border sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable only when they knowingly directed or authorised the AML breach. For active participation in money laundering or terrorist financing, the Criminal Code imposes imprisonment up to 10 years (money laundering). Courts may issue travel bans pending the criminal case, order restitution, and in serious cases permit the forfeiture of personal and corporate assets traceable to the unlawful activity.
